confirmed_defects.regression: No. The frozen combined submission (nested RA source, SHA-256 dec028b0...) gives the same result. The RB-01 correction text I wrote said to examine an ancestor only when 'its head is not removed'. The delivered code implements that condition as written, and this route passes through it. The gap is in my specified correction as much as in the code.
confirmed_defects.title: A late supersession link is not honoured when the locked ancestor was withdrawn after the lock
source: accounting_agent/source_control.py source_origin lines 124-127: the ancestor loop looks only at ancestors whose head is not removed. A head removed by a withdrawal that arrived under the lock is skipped, although that withdrawal was itself quarantined (LATE_ACTIVITY_IN_LOCKED_PERIOD) and the charge is still approved in the locked population.
accounting_agent/source_control.py source_origin lines 128-130: the fallback then returns the source's own earlier December admission.
accounting_agent/service.py bind_source lines 219-227: the origin so resolved is the destination period, so nothing is moved or blocked.
accounting_agent/service.py change_period_status line 185: on reopen, removed heads are skipped, so a withdrawal quarantined under the lock is never admitted afterwards.
minimal_reproduction: Approve A1 (3 Nov, 40.00) and lock November; December is open.
Intake B1 dated 2 Dec, 40.00, with its receipt and a December statement, with no supersession claim. It is admitted to December and is eligible.
Intake A1 again with tombstone true and removal_reason 'voided'. November is locked, so the withdrawal is quarantined.
Re-send B1 with supersedes='demo_card_001:A1'. Run December card preparation.
Disposition SOURCE_TRANSITION_REQUIRES_REVIEW as settlement_verified citing the whole evidence list. Re-run. An independent reviewer approves B1. Finalize December without acknowledgement.
Control: the same three sources with the withdrawal first and B1 arriving with its claim are quarantined correctly.
confirmed_defects.expected: B1 and its receipt are quarantined under November with SOURCE_MOVED_FROM_LOCKED_PERIOD and B1 leaves the December population, as happens when the claim arrives with B1.
confirmed_defects.actual: B1 stays governing in December with only SOURCE_TRANSITION_REQUIRES_REVIEW, is dispositioned and approved. A1 remains approved in locked November. December finalizes without acknowledgement. state.source_exceptions is empty and no move row is recorded. The only trace is the pair of events APPROVED_SOURCE_REMOVED and APPROVED_SOURCE_SUPERSEDED on A1.
confirmed_defects.accounting_or_control_consequence: The same expense and liability are approved in two periods, one locked. A provider that voids the original row, delivers the replacement and declares the link in a later delivery produces it without any unusual intent.
smallest_sufficient_correction: In source_origin, in the ancestor loop, also treat an ancestor as held by the lock when its head is removed and the head snapshot's latest binding is not admitted, has reason LATE_ACTIVITY_IN_LOCKED_PERIOD and names a period that is still locked. Return that period as the blocking origin.

In change_period_status on reopen, also re-bind a removed head whose latest binding is LATE_ACTIVITY_IN_LOCKED_PERIOD in the reopened period, so that the withdrawal is admitted once the period is open. Without this, the first change would wrongly block a destination revision after a valid release and relock.

List a withdrawal quarantined under a lock in state.source_exceptions. Today the query hides every source whose head is removed (service.py state, source_exceptions), so the withdrawal of an approved locked charge is shown only as an event.

state.source_exceptions lists the quarantined withdrawal of A1 under November.
After reopening November and re-preparing both periods: November has no governing A1, December has exactly one governing item for the charge carrying SOURCE_TRANSITION_REQUIRES_REVIEW.
After a relock of November, a later revision of B1 stays in December (probes R01a and N01a relock steps unchanged).
regression_tests: new unit tests: withdrawal under lock then late link; the same after reopen and relock

source: accounting_agent/source_control.py source_revision line 53 and accounting_agent/service.py intake lines 380-382: after an intake, bind_source is called for the source taken in and for every receipt, but not for other live transactions whose supersession chain has just changed.

minimal_reproduction: Approve A1 (3 Nov, 40.00) and lock November; December is open.
Intake B1 dated 2 Dec, 40.00, with its receipt and a December statement that names C1, with no supersession claim.
Intake C1 dated 3 Dec, 40.00, with its receipt and supersedes='demo_card_001:B1'. C1 replaces B1 inside December. Variant: disposition and approve C1 now.
Re-send B1 with supersedes='demo_card_001:A1'. Run December card preparation.
Disposition SOURCE_TRANSITION_REQUIRES_REVIEW on C1 as settlement_verified, re-run, and an independent reviewer approves C1.
confirmed_defects.expected: C1 and its receipt are quarantined under November together with B1, because C1 replaces B1 and B1 replaces the locked A1.
confirmed_defects.actual: Only B1 is quarantined. C1 stays the governing December item. Where C1 had been approved, that approval is displaced and an independent reviewer approves the new version directly; where it had not, it is dispositioned and approved. A1 remains approved in locked November.
confirmed_defects.accounting_or_control_consequence: The same expense and liability are approved in two periods, one locked. The December reviewer sees the chain C1 -> B1 -> A1 in the evidence list but no blocker that says the root is locked.
smallest_sufficient_correction: After every intake that changed anything, re-bind every live transaction head that has a supersession chain, shortest chain first, before the existing receipt loop (service.py intake, lines 380-382). bind_source is idempotent for a source whose situation has not changed.

A replacement whose chain now contains an ancestor held by a lock is quarantined by the existing source_origin ancestor loop; its approval, if any, is reported by the existing approved-source event and ITEM_LEFT_POPULATION.

source: accounting_agent/source_control.py source_revision lines 47-48: a claim whose target has not been received records only the event SOURCE_SUPERSESSION_UNRESOLVED. No link is created then, and none is created when the target later arrives (links are written only at lines 49-50, at the claimant's own intake).
accounting_agent/source_control.py supersession_refs lines 62-70: the chain of a later replacement therefore stops at the claimant.

accounting_agent/service.py context lines 259-261: the unresolved flag is shown only while the claimant's snapshot is in the period population; once the claimant is itself replaced, the flag disappears.

Intake A1Y dated 3 Dec, 40.00, with its receipt, supersedes='demo_card_001:A1X' (not yet received), and a December statement that names A1Z. A1Y is admitted to December and held as unresolved.
Intake A1X dated 2 Dec with its receipt and supersedes='demo_card_001:A1'. It is quarantined under November.

confirmed_defects.expected: A1Y is linked to A1X as soon as A1X exists and is quarantined; A1Z, which replaces A1Y, is quarantined with it. This is what happens when A1Y is re-sent (probe R01c).

confirmed_defects.accounting_or_control_consequence: The same expense and liability are approved in two periods, one locked. Whether the control holds depends on whether the provider happens to re-send a row.
smallest_sufficient_correction: After every intake that changed anything, and before the re-evaluation step of RC-02, resolve recorded claims: for each SOURCE_SUPERSESSION_UNRESOLVED event whose claimant snapshot is still the head of its key (removed or not), which has no link yet, and whose target key now has a head, insert the link (unless it would close a cycle) and emit the same APPROVED_SOURCE_SUPERSEDED events as at line 51-52.
In context (service.py lines 259-261), stop reporting a claim as unresolved once its snapshot has a link.
The re-evaluation step of RC-02 then quarantines the claimant and every live source that replaces it.

It fails in the safe direction. A route for accepting a statement revision without an item is needed before a real zero-activity cycle.

When a statement is withdrawn and replaced, the workpaper lists the replacement twice, once against the original version and once against the withdrawal version of the old key. Cosmetic.

decisions_requiring_client_authority: Feed semantics (gate G2): whether a provider can void a row in a closed cycle, deliver a replacement before the row it replaces, or declare a link in a later delivery; and whether a removed replacement restores the original.

Document policy: date window, amount tolerance, multiple receipts, who may re-attach or withdraw a receipt, whether withdrawal of contradicting evidence must be disclosed (UC-10), and who may accept a corrected or replaced receipt.

Statement policy: which document is authoritative, who may supply or correct it, how cycles map to periods, how a correction to a closed cycle is carried forward, and how a revision of a statement with no activity is accepted (UC-11).
Whether the person who approves or writes policy may also review items prepared under it (currently barred).
Treatment of fees, interest, card payments and transfers, and the accounts each disposition may use.
The close checklist, the evidence each line requires, and who gives final sign-off.
Who may disposition, finalize and lock, and what evidence must be new before a recurring run.
